mainTopic: Wounding a daughter, and a Canaanite slave's status as a 'brother': בושת, kingship, and why a slave cannot testify
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge about a father who wounds his young daughter. רבי אלעזר's doubt was only about payments that lower her value, and רבי יוסי בר חנינא answers that the wound was on her face, so it did lower her value. The גמרא then explains why רבי יהודה says someone who injures a Canaanite slave pays no בושת: the פסוק says 'his brother,' and a slave is not a brother. The חכמים reply that a slave is a brother in מצוות. Challenges follow from עדים זוממין, from kingship and from testimony, and each is answered: 'remove the evil from your midst' includes every case, and a king must come from the choicest of the brothers. To show that a slave cannot testify, the גמרא tries עולא's קל וחומר from a woman, then a minor, then a robber, and settles on a robber combined with a woman or a minor. מר בריה דרבינא brings a different source, the פסוק 'fathers shall not be put to death for children,' which excludes a slave but not a convert, who still has family below him. Finally the גמרא returns to the משנה about a deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person and a minor, and begins a story about a woman who signed her property over to her son. That story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's doubt was only about payments that lower her value
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the point that רבי אלעזר only had a doubt about בושת, because it lowers the girl's value. A wound does not lower her value, so he had no doubt about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...since it lowered her monetary value. But a wound, which did not lower her monetary value, he did not have a doubt about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a sentence from the earlier discussion. It limits רבי אלעזר's doubt to payments that make the girl worth less money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Embarrassment (בושת) can lower how much a father will receive at his daughter's betrothal, so whether her father keeps that payment is an open question. A plain wound does not affect that money, so רבי אלעזר never asked about it. This distinction makes the case of a wound look unconnected to his doubt, and that sets up the next line.

keyTerms.meaning: He lowered her monetary value (what her father would get for her betrothal)
He had a doubt / raised a question about it

phrases.english: since he lowered her monetary value;
but a wound, which did not lower her monetary value,
he did not have a doubt about it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל פְּצִיעָה דְּלָא אַפְחֲתַהּ מִכַּסְפַּהּ לָא קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from the previous daf about wounding one's young daughter
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Limits רבי אלעזר's doubt to payments that lower the girl's value
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A plain wound does not lower her value, so it seems to fall outside his doubt

steps.title: The wound was on her face, so it did lower her value
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא explains that the case is a wound on the girl's face. Such a wound does lower her value.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: It is a case where he wounded her on her face, and so he lowered her monetary value.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר חנינא answers the challenge by explaining that the ruling of רבי יוחנן from the previous amud is about a wound on the girl's face.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wound on the face can make a girl worth less at betrothal, just as embarrassment can. So this wound also falls into the group of payments that lower her value. That closes the gap raised in the previous line.

keyTerms.meaning: That he wounded her on her face

steps.whatToRemember: A wound counts as lowering the girl's value when it is on her face, since that affects what her father receives at her betrothal.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina said:
It is where he wounded her on her face,
and so he lowered her monetary value.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא שֶׁפְּצָעָהּ בְּפָנֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the gap from step 1 by defining the wound as one that lowers her value
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A wound never lowers the girl's value
steps.terutzMaskana: A wound on the face does lower her value, so it fits the same group as בושת

steps.title: What is רבי יהודה's reason for exempting a slave from embarrassment payment?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about injuring someone else's Canaanite slave. It asks why רבי יהודה says there is no בושת payment for a slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: One who injures another person's Canaanite slave is liable for all five payments, and so on. What is the reasoning of רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the משנה and asks where רבי יהודה's view comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's first opinion holds that the injurer pays all five payments, even for a slave. רבי יהודה says a slave has no בושת. The גמרא wants a source for his exemption.

keyTerms.meaning: A Canaanite (non-Jewish) slave owned by a Jew
Etc., the rest of the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree that the injurer pays for damage, pain, healing and lost work. The only argument is about בושת (embarrassment).

phrases.english: One who injures a Canaanite slave belonging to others
is liable, etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of the משנה: רבי יהודה says slaves have no בושת.

phrases.english: What is the reasoning of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the next line of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for רבי יהודה's ruling that a slave has no בושת

steps.title: The verse says 'his brother', and a slave is not a brother
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק about בושת says 'a man and his brother.' This teaches that the law applies only to someone who has 'brotherhood,' which leaves out a slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'When men fight together, a man and his brother.' This teaches that the law applies to someone who has brotherhood, which leaves out a slave, who has no brotherhood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יהודה's source: the word 'his brother' in the פסוק about בושת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The section about embarrassment payment opens with 'a man and his brother.' רבי יהודה reads 'brother' as a limit: the law covers only someone who counts as a fellow Jew in this sense. A Canaanite slave does not have that status, so there is no בושת for him.

phrases.english: The verse says:
"When men fight together,
a man and his brother"
— this applies to someone who has brotherhood,
leaving out a slave, who has no brotherhood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא כִּי יִנָּצוּ אֲנָשִׁים יַחְדָּו אִישׁ וְאָחִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'his brother' limits בושת to someone who has brotherhood, which leaves out a slave

steps.title: The חכמים: a slave is a brother in מצוות
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that a slave counts as a 'brother,' because he shares in keeping מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: he is his brother in מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the חכמים read the same word 'brother' differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים agree that the פסוק requires a 'brother.' However, they hold that a Canaanite slave is a brother because he is obligated in מצוות. So he is included in בושת.

keyTerms.meaning: He is his brother with regard to מצוות

phrases.english: And the Rabbis: he is his brother with regard to מצוות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the חכמים' reading of the same word that רבי יהודה used in step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Brother' includes a slave, since he shares in מצוות

steps.title: Then false witnesses against a slave should not be executed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה. The פסוק about עדים זוממין also says 'his brother,' so by his reasoning, false witnesses against a slave would never be punished with death.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, according to רבי יהודה, false witnesses who testified against a slave should not be executed, since it is written: 'You shall do to him as he plotted to do to his brother'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יהודה's reasoning by applying it to another פסוק that uses the same word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The law of עדים זוממין says they receive the punishment they 'plotted to do to his brother.' If a slave is not a 'brother,' witnesses who falsely tried to get a slave executed would escape punishment. That result seems wrong, so his reading of 'brother' looks hard to accept.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (a formula that starts a challenge)

phrases.english: But if so, according to Rabbi Yehuda,
false witnesses against a slave should not be executed,
as it is written:
"You shall do to him as he plotted
to do to his brother"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה זוֹמְמֵי עֶבֶד לֹא יֵהָרְגוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יהודה's reading of 'brother' from step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's rule that 'brother' leaves out a slave
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word appears in the law of עדים זוממין, so false witnesses against a slave would go unpunished, which seems unacceptable

steps.title: 'Remove the evil from your midst' includes every case
steps.stepSummary: רבא, quoting רב ששת, answers that the same section also says 'and you shall remove the evil from your midst.' This phrase teaches that false witnesses are punished in every case, including testimony against a slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב ששת: The verse says, 'And you shall remove the evil from your midst,' which means in every case.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge for רבי יהודה by pointing to an extra phrase in the section about עדים זוממין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'His brother' alone would leave out a slave. However, 'remove the evil from your midst' is a general phrase, so the punishment covers witnesses against a slave too. רבי יהודה's reading of 'brother' still applies to בושת, where no such extra phrase appears.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall remove the evil from your midst
In any case / no matter what
A Babylonian אמורא, quoted here by רבא

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, 'brother' leaves out a slave for בושת. For עדים זוממין, the phrase 'remove the evil from your midst' adds a slave back in.

phrases.english: Rava said that Rav Sheshet said:
The verse says:
"And you shall remove the evil from your midst"
— in any case.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר קְרָא וּבִעַרְתָּ הָרָע מִקִּרְבֶּךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to another phrase in the פסוק that widens the law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a slave is not a 'brother,' false witnesses against him would go free
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Remove the evil from your midst' includes every case, so false witnesses against a slave are executed

steps.title: Should a slave be fit to be king?
steps.stepSummary: If the רבנן count a slave as a 'brother,' then the פסוק about appointing a king 'from among your brothers' should allow a slave to be king.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, according to the רבנן, a slave should be fit to be king!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the חכמים. If a slave counts as a 'brother,' he should also be allowed to be king.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about a king says 'from among your brothers.' The חכמים just said a slave is a 'brother' because he keeps מצוות. So by their logic, a slave should qualify for kingship, and that sounds clearly wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so, now that you say this (introduces a challenge built on what was just said)
The Sages, here the חכמים who argue with רבי יהודה

phrases.english: But if so, according to the Rabbis –
a slave should be fit for kingship!
phrases.notes: The גמרא is thinking of the פסוק 'from among your brothers shall you set a king over you' (דברים 17:15).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רבי יהודה's view and now attacks the חכמים' claim from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים' claim that a slave counts as 'brother'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'brother' includes a slave, the kingship פסוק that uses 'brothers' would allow a slave to be king, which is unacceptable.

steps.title: The same question applies to a convert for everyone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא replies (אָמְרִי, 'they say') in defense of the רבנן that the challenge proves too much: a convert is surely a 'brother' to everyone, yet a convert cannot be king.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: And according to your reasoning, a convert should be a difficulty for you according to everyone!
steps.whatsHappening: An anonymous answer (אָמְרִי) defends the חכמים by turning the challenge around. Even רבי יהודה agrees a convert is a 'brother,' yet a convert cannot be king.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the kingship rule cannot be based on who is a 'brother.' The question is not a special problem for the חכמים. Everyone needs a different explanation, and the גמרא gives it in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning (turns the question back on the asker)

phrases.english: They say: And according to your reasoning,
a convert should be difficult for you –
phrases.notes: A convert certainly counts as a 'brother,' yet he cannot be king. So how would you explain that?

phrases.english: according to everyone!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defuses step 8 by showing that the same problem exists for everyone.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counter-question (ולטעמיך): the question applies to all opinions, so it cannot be aimed at the רבנן alone
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The kingship rule depends only on being a 'brother,' so a slave who counts as a brother should qualify.
steps.terutzMaskana: A convert is a brother and still cannot be king, so kingship must depend on something more than being a brother.

steps.title: A king must come from the choicest of the brothers
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק's words 'מקרב אחיך' teach that a king must come from the choicest of the brothers, which leaves out both convert and slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the פסוק says 'from among your brothers,' which means from the choicest among your brothers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real reason a slave or convert cannot be king. The word 'מקרב' teaches that the king must come from the best of the brothers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being a 'brother' is not enough for kingship. There is an extra requirement of being 'choice.' So the חכמים can keep calling a slave a 'brother' without making him fit to be king.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק says (introduces a source from a פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: Kingship needs more than being a 'brother.' It needs the 'choicest' of the brothers, so a slave and a convert are both excluded, even for the חכמים.

phrases.english: Rather, the verse says:
"From among your brothers" –
from the choicest among your brothers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the true source that step 9 showed was needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reading of the פסוק: 'מקרב' adds a requirement of being choice
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the choicest of the brothers can be king, which excludes a convert and a slave.

steps.title: Should a slave be fit to testify?
steps.stepSummary: The עדים זוממין פסוק says the false witness testified against 'his brother,' so if a slave is a brother, he should be a valid witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, according to the רבנן, a slave should be fit to testify, as it is written: 'And behold, the witness is a false witness; he testified falsely against his brother'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a second challenge to the חכמים. If a slave is a 'brother,' the witness פסוק suggests he should be allowed to testify.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls the witness the 'brother' of the person he testified against. That implies witnesses are 'brothers.' If a slave is a 'brother,' nothing here would stop him from being a witness.

phrases.english: But if so, according to the Rabbis –
a slave should be fit for testimony,
as it is written: "And behold, the witness is a false witness,
he testified falsely against his brother"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, לְרַבָּנַן – יְהֵא עֶבֶד כָּשֵׁר לְעֵדוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second attack on the חכמים, built the same way as step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים' claim that a slave counts as 'brother'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The witness פסוק treats witnesses as 'brothers.' If a slave is a brother, he should be able to testify, but he cannot.

steps.title: עולא: a קל וחומר from a woman disqualifies a slave
steps.stepSummary: A woman may marry into the community and still cannot testify, so a slave, who cannot marry into the community, surely cannot testify.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: You cannot say a slave can testify, because his testimony is learned by a קל וחומר from a woman. A woman can marry into the community and is still unfit to testify. A slave cannot marry into the community, so surely he is unfit to testify.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers that a slave's unfitness to testify comes from a separate source, a קל וחומר from a woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being a 'brother' does not decide who can testify. A woman has a higher status, since she can marry into the community, yet she still cannot testify. So a slave, with a lower status, surely cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter one
To enter the congregation, meaning to marry a Jew of proper lineage
Is it not logical? (the closing formula of a קל וחומר)

phrases.english: Ulla said:
Testimony, you cannot say;
testimony is derived by an a fortiori argument from a woman:
Just as a woman,
who is fit to enter the congregation –
is disqualified from testimony;
a slave, who is not fit to enter the congregation –
is it not logical that he is disqualified from testimony?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: עֵדוּת לָא מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A separate source (קל וחומר) overrides the implication of the word 'brother'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a slave is a 'brother,' he should be able to testify.
steps.terutzMaskana: A slave is disqualified from testimony through a קל וחומר from a woman.

steps.title: A woman cannot have מילה, but a slave can
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר is attacked: perhaps a woman is unfit to testify because she has no מילה, and a slave does have מילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a woman? She is not fit for מילה. Would you say the same about a slave, who is fit for מילה?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges עולא's קל וחומר by finding a way a slave is 'better' than a woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the source case is stronger in every relevant way. A slave has the מצוה of מילה, and a woman does not. So maybe that is why a woman cannot testify, and the reason would not apply to a slave.

keyTerms.meaning: What about...? (a formula pointing out a weakness in a קל וחומר)

phrases.english: What about a woman –
since she is not fit for circumcision;
would you say so of a slave, who is fit for circumcision?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְאִשָּׁה – שֶׁכֵּן אֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה לְמִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the קל וחומר of step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's קל וחומר from a woman
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source case, a woman, has a weakness the slave lacks, since she has no מילה. That breaks the קל וחומר.

steps.title: A minor proves that מילה does not matter
steps.stepSummary: A קטן has מילה and still cannot testify, so מילה is not what makes someone fit to testify.
steps.simpleTranslation: A minor proves it: he has מילה, and he is still unfit to testify.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends עולא's קל וחומר by showing that the מילה point does not matter for testimony.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If having מילה made someone fit to testify, a קטן would be fit, and he is not. So the difference between a woman and a slave regarding מילה does not affect testimony, and the קל וחומר stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Will prove (shows that a suggested difference is not relevant)

steps.whatToRemember: For the חכמים, a slave counts as a 'brother,' but he still cannot be king, because a king must be 'choice.' His unfitness to testify comes from a separate source. Steps 15–21 test עולא's קל וחומר until it is settled by combining a גזלן with an אשה or a קטן.

phrases.english: A minor will prove it –
for he is included in circumcision,
and he is disqualified from testimony.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13 and protects the קל וחומר of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: יוכיח: a counterexample shows that the suggested difference is not relevant
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Perhaps having מילה makes a person fit to testify, so a slave would differ from a woman.
steps.terutzMaskana: A קטן has מילה and still cannot testify, so מילה is not relevant and the קל וחומר holds.

steps.title: A minor is different because he has no מצוות
steps.stepSummary: The proof from a קטן is rejected: a קטן is not obligated in מצוות, but an עבד is.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is a minor unfit? Because he is not obligated in מצוות. Can you say the same about a slave, who is obligated in מצוות?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the proof from a קטן in step 14. It finds a different reason why a קטן cannot testify.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 showed that having מילה does not make someone fit to testify, because a קטן has מילה and still cannot testify. But maybe a קטן is unfit because he has no מצוות at all. An עבד is obligated in מצוות, so he might still be fit.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What about X... would you say the same about Y?' This is the standard way to show that two cases are different.
Commandments; here, being obligated to keep them
A minor, a child under the age of מצוות

phrases.english: What about a minor? He is not obligated in מצוות;
would you say the same about a slave, who is obligated in מצוות?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from a קטן in step 14 by giving a different reason for his being unfit.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of a קטן to show that מילה does not make someone fit to testify
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קטן may be unfit because he has no obligation in מצוות. An עבד does have that obligation, so the comparison fails.

steps.title: A woman proves that מצוות are not the deciding factor
steps.stepSummary: An אשה is obligated in מצוות and still cannot testify, so being obligated in מצוות does not make someone fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman proves it: she is obligated in מצוות, and she is still unfit to testify.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 15 by pointing to an אשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 said that being obligated in מצוות might make an עבד fit. But an אשה is obligated in מצוות and is still unfit to testify. So that cannot be the reason a person is fit.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Will prove.' One case shows that a suggested reason does not work.

phrases.english: A woman will prove it:
she is obligated in מצוות, and she is unfit to testify.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 by bringing back the אשה as a counterexample.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe being obligated in מצוות makes an עבד fit to testify.
steps.terutzMaskana: An אשה is obligated in מצוות and is still unfit, so that reason does not work.

steps.title: Combining woman and minor through what they share
steps.stepSummary: Each case can be pushed aside alone, so the גמרא combines them. Both the אשה and the קטן are not obligated in all the מצוות and cannot testify, and the same is true of an עבד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The argument has gone back and forth. This case is not like that one, and that case is not like this one. What they share is that neither is obligated in all the מצוות, and both are unfit to testify. So I will also include the slave, who is not obligated in all the מצוות, and he is unfit to testify.
steps.whatsHappening: The אשה was rejected in step 13 and the קטן was rejected in step 15. So the גמרא now builds one combined proof from the feature they both share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Alone, each case has its own weak spot: an אשה has no מילה, and a קטן has no מצוות. Together, those weak spots cancel out. What is left is what they share: neither is obligated in all the מצוות. An עבד shares that feature, so he should also be unfit.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The argument has come back around.' Both single cases have been knocked down, so we start again.
'The look of this one is not like the look of that one.' Each case has its own separate feature.
The shared feature of two cases, used to learn the law for a third case

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 15. There the point was having no מצוות at all, which is true only of a קטן. Here the shared point is not being obligated in ALL the מצוות, which is true of both an אשה and a קטן.

phrases.english: And the argument has come back around:
this case is not like that case,
and that case is not like this case;
what they have in common

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן אֵינָן בְּכׇל הַמִּצְוֹת, וּפְסוּלִין לְהָעִיד;
phrases.english: is that they are not obligated in all the מצוות, and they are unfit to testify;
so I will also include the slave,
who is not obligated in all the מצוות, and so he is unfit to testify.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחָזַר הַדִּין: לֹא רְאִי זֶה כִרְאִי זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines the two cases that were each rejected into a single shared-feature proof.
steps.raayaObject: That an עבד is unfit to testify
steps.raayaSupportSource: A הצד השוה drawn from אשה and קטן: neither is obligated in all the מצוות, and both are unfit to testify.

steps.title: Woman and minor are not grown men
steps.stepSummary: The הצד השוה is rejected: an אשה and a קטן also share that neither is an איש, a grown man, while an עבד is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about what they have in common? Neither of them is a grown man. Would you say the same about a slave, who is a grown man?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the combined proof from step 17. It finds another feature that the אשה and the קטן share but the עבד does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשה and a קטן have a second thing in common: neither is an איש, a grown man. Maybe that is why they cannot testify. An עבד is a grown man, so the combined proof does not reach him.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Since,' 'in that.' It introduces the special feature that makes a case different.

phrases.english: What about what they have in common?
Neither of them is a grown man;
would you say the same about a slave, who is a grown man?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the הצד השוה proof from step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The הצד השוה proof from אשה and קטן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two cases share another feature, not being a grown man. That feature does not apply to an עבד, so the proof does not reach him.

steps.title: Try learning from a robber instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a new source: learn from a גזלן, who cannot testify even though he is a grown man.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn it from a robber.
steps.whatsHappening: The אשה and קטן route has failed, so the גמרא tries a new source. A גזלן is a grown man and still cannot testify.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 suggested that being a grown man makes someone fit to testify. A גזלן is a grown man, yet he is unfit. So maybe an עבד can be learned from him.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather.' It drops the earlier approach and offers a new one.
'Let it come from,' meaning let us learn it from
A robber, who is unfit to testify

phrases.english: Rather, learn it from a robber.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the failed אשה and קטן proof and offers a new source.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Being a grown man may make an עבד fit to testify.
steps.terutzMaskana: A גזלן is a grown man and is still unfit, so an עבד could be learned from him.

steps.title: A robber brought it on himself
steps.stepSummary: The proof from a גזלן is rejected: his own sins made him unfit, but an עבד did nothing wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a robber? His own actions caused him to be unfit. Would you say the same about a slave, whose actions did not cause him to be unfit?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from a גזלן in step 19. The next step answers this by combining sources.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזלן is unfit because of what he did, as a kind of penalty. An עבד is unfit, if at all, because of his status and not because he did anything wrong. A law based on punishment cannot be carried over to someone who did no wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: 'His own actions caused it.' He brought the unfitness on himself.

steps.whatToRemember: Every attempted source so far (אשה, קטן, both combined, and גזלן) has been rejected. Each one has its own special reason for being unfit that does not apply to an עבד.

phrases.english: What about a robber?
His own actions caused him to be unfit;
would you say the same about a slave,
whose own actions did not cause him to be unfit?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְגַזְלָן – שֶׁכֵּן מַעֲשָׂיו גָּרְמוּ לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from a גזלן in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from a גזלן that an עבד is unfit to testify
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גזלן is unfit because of his own sins. An עבד committed no sin, so the reason does not carry over.

steps.title: Combine a robber with a woman or a minor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא learns the עבד from a combination of a גזלן and either an אשה or a קטן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn it from a robber together with one of those two (a woman or a minor).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the broken proofs by pairing the גזלן with an אשה or a קטן, so each one covers the other's weakness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אשה and the קטן alone fail because neither is a grown man, but the גזלן is a grown man. The גזלן alone fails because his own sins made him unfit, but the אשה or קטן did nothing wrong. What they share is that none of them keeps all the מצוות and none can testify, and the same is true of an עבד.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it come / learn it from
A robber, who cannot be a witness
One of those (the אשה or the קטן)

steps.whatToRemember: The final הצד השוה pairs a גזלן with an אשה or a קטן. Each one answers the challenge that was raised against the other.

phrases.english: Rather, derive it from a robber
and from one of these
phrases.notes: "These" means the אשה or the קטן from the earlier steps.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection in step 20 by combining the גזלן with an אשה or a קטן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Combined הצד השוה: each source covers the other's weakness
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גזלן alone fails because his unfitness comes from sin.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גזלן plus an אשה or a קטן share that none keeps all the מצוות and none can testify, so an עבד is unfit too.

steps.title: A new source from the verse about fathers and children
steps.stepSummary: מר בריה דרבינא reads ״לֹא יוּמְתוּ אָבוֹת עַל בָּנִים״ as excluding the testimony of fathers with no family link to their children.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בריה דרבינא said: the פסוק says ״fathers shall not be put to death for children.″ This means no one is put to death through the testimony of fathers who have no family link to their children.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא gives a completely different source, from a פסוק, for why an עבד cannot testify.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the פסוק as being about witnesses: no one is executed על פי, through the word of, such fathers. A father whose children are not counted as related to him is an עבד. So an עבד's testimony is not accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: מר, the son of רבינא, an אמורא

steps.confusionAlert: Read simply, this פסוק is about punishing a person for a relative's sin. Here it is read as a rule about who may testify.

phrases.english: Mar, son of Ravina, said:
The verse states:
"Fathers shall not be put to death for children"
meaning: people shall not be put to death by the testimony of fathers
who have no family lineage with their children.
phrases.notes: This is talking about an עבד, whose children aren't counted as his relatives.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבִינָא אָמַר, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a separate source from a פסוק instead of the הצד השוה reasoning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק excludes the testimony of a father with no family link to his children, meaning an עבד.

steps.title: Proof from the missing word "their"
steps.stepSummary: If the פסוק simply meant a father testifying about his own children, it would say "their children." Since it just says "children," it must mean fathers who have no family link to children.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you thought the פסוק means, as we usually explain it, that fathers are not killed through their children's testimony, then the Torah should have written ״their children.″ Why does it say just ״children″? Learn from this that it means fathers who have no family link to children.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בריה דרבינא backs up his reading by pointing to an exact word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual reading is that relatives cannot testify about each other. That reading would fit better with the wording "their children." The plain word "children" points to fathers who are not linked to children at all, which is an עבד.

keyTerms.meaning: If it enters your mind (if you thought)
Let the Torah (the Merciful One) write

phrases.english: For if you think it means as we usually say:
"Fathers shall not be put to death for children"
meaning by the testimony of their children,
then let the Merciful One write:
"Fathers shall not be put to death for their children"!
Why does it just say "children"?
Learn from this that people shall not be put to death

phrases.aramaic: עַל פִּי אָבוֹת שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חַיִיס בָּנִים.
phrases.english: by the testimony of fathers who have no family lineage with children.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the דרשה of step 22 from the exact wording of the פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That the פסוק is about fathers with no family link (an עבד), not simply about relatives.

steps.title: Then a convert should also be unfit
steps.stepSummary: Using the same reading on the second half of the פסוק would mean children with no family link to their fathers cannot testify. That would make a גר unfit, which is clearly wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, then ״and children shall not be put to death for fathers″ should also mean: not through the testimony of children who have no family link to their fathers. Then a גר should also be unfit to testify?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new דרשה by applying the same method to the other half of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second half of the פסוק also has no word for "their." So it should exclude children who have no link to their fathers. A גר has no family link to his parents, so he would be unfit to testify, but a גר is fit.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so, from now on (by that logic)

phrases.english: But if that is so,
"and children shall not be put to death for fathers"
phrases.notes: This is the next part of the same פסוק, דברים 24:16.

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי נָמֵי, לֹא יוּמְתוּ עַל פִּי בָּנִים
phrases.english: does it also mean: not put to death by the testimony of children
who have no family lineage with fathers?
But then a convert would also be
unfit for testimony?!
phrases.notes: A גר is no longer counted as related to his non-Jewish parents.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, ״וּבָנִים לֹא יוּמְתוּ עַל אָבוֹת״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the דרשה of steps 22-23 by applying the same method to the second half of the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The דרשה of מר בריה דרבינא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same reading of the second half would disqualify a גר, who has no family link to his parents, yet a גר is a valid witness.

steps.title: A convert still has family below him
steps.stepSummary: A גר has no family link to his parents but does have one to his children. An עבד has no family link in either direction.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: how can you compare them? A גר may have no family link above him, but below him he does. This comes to exclude an עבד, who has no family link either above or below.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the דרשה by showing that a גר is different from an עבד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse only excludes someone with no family link at all. A גר is still linked to his own children, so he is fit. An עבד has no recognized link to parents or to children, so he alone is excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (these are not alike)

steps.whatToRemember: According to מר בריה דרבינא, an עבד cannot testify because he has no family link at all, neither to parents nor to children. A גר keeps a link to his children, so he can testify.
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains why the source that disqualifies an עבד does not also disqualify a גר, who is a fully valid witness.

phrases.english: They say: how can these be compared?!

phrases.aramaic: גֵּר, נְהִי דְּאֵין לוֹ חַיִיס לְמַעְלָה,
phrases.english: A convert, granted he has no lineage above him,
phrases.notes: "Above" means his parents, and "below" means his children.

phrases.english: below him he does have lineage;
this excludes a slave,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאֵין לוֹ חַיִיס לֹא לְמַעְלָה וְלֹא לְמַטָּה.
phrases.english: who has no lineage either above or below.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24 by showing how a גר differs from an עבד.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A גר has no family link to his parents, so the דרשה should make him unfit.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only someone with no family link at all, above or below, is excluded, and that is an עבד.

steps.title: If a convert were unfit, the verse would be worded differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins proving that a גר is fit to testify. If he were unfit, the Torah should have written ״עַל בְּנֵיהֶם״ in the first half and left the second half as ״עַל אָבוֹת״, which would teach the גר's unfitness.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think a גר cannot testify, the Torah should have written 'Fathers shall not be put to death for their children', meaning fathers are not killed through their children's testimony. Then 'Nor shall children be put to death for fathers' would teach two things: children are not killed through their fathers' testimony, and people are not killed through the testimony of 'children' who have no family link to fathers, meaning converts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a proof that a גר is a valid witness. It shows how the Torah would have worded the פסוק if a גר were unfit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 said a גר has a family link to his children but not to his parents. Here the גמרא argues: if that were enough to make him unfit, the second half of the פסוק, ״וּבָנִים לֹא יוּמְתוּ עַל אָבוֹת״, could carry that lesson, and the first half would say ״בְּנֵיהֶם״ to mean only a father's own children. The Torah did not word it that way, and the next steps explain what that tells us.

keyTerms.meaning: It would enter your mind, meaning: if you were to think
Unfit to testify as a witness
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah or ה׳

steps.confusionAlert: The Torah does NOT actually say ״עַל בְּנֵיהֶם״. The גמרא is describing how the פסוק would have looked if a גר were unfit, in order to prove that he is not.

phrases.english: For if it would enter your mind
that a convert is unfit to testify,
then let the Merciful One write:
"Fathers shall not be put to death for their children"
phrases.notes: The real פסוק (דברים 24:16) just says 'children'. This is how the Torah would have worded it.

phrases.english: to teach what we said:
fathers are not put to death through the testimony of their children;
and let the Merciful One write:
"Nor shall children be put to death for fathers"
from which you would learn two things:

phrases.aramaic: חֲדָא – לֹא יוּמְתוּ בָּנִים בְּעֵדוּת אָבוֹת,
phrases.english: One: children are not put to death through their fathers' testimony,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִידַּךְ – לֹא יוּמְתוּ עַל פִּי בָּנִים
phrases.english: and the other: people are not put to death through the testimony of children
who have no family link to fathers!
phrases.notes: That's a גר, who isn't counted as related to his parents.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ גֵּר פָּסוּל לְעֵדוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the answer in step 25 by proving that a גר is actually fit to testify.
steps.raayaObject: That a גר is fit to testify
steps.raayaSupportSource: The exact wording of ״לֹא יוּמְתוּ אָבוֹת עַל בָּנִים״ (דברים 24:16), compared with how it would have been worded if a גר were unfit

steps.title: Under that wording, the slave would come from a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The proof continues. If a גר were unfit, the עבד would not need his own lesson from the פסוק, because it would follow by a קל וחומר: if a גר, who has a family link downward, is unfit, then an עבד, who has none at all, is surely unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the עבד would be learned by a קל וחומר from the גר. A גר has no family link upward, but he does have one downward, and still he would be unfit. An עבד has no family link upward or downward, so surely he is unfit to testify.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the proof. Under the imagined wording, the עבד's unfitness would come from logic alone, not from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that the imagined wording would cover everything: the גר from the second half of the פסוק, and the עבד by a קל וחומר from the גר. Because nothing would be missing, the fact that the Torah chose a different wording must teach something else.

keyTerms.meaning: He derives it, or it comes out from
A 'how much more so' argument, from a lighter case to a stricter one

phrases.english: And a slave would be derived
by a קל וחומר from a convert:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה גֵּר, דִּלְמַעְלָה הוּא דְּאֵין לוֹ חַיִיס,
phrases.english: If a convert, who has no family link only upward,
but downward does have a family link,
is unfit to testify,
then a slave, who has no family link
neither upward nor downward,
isn't it logical that he should be unfit to testify?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעֶבֶד – נָפְקָא לֵיהּ בְּקַל וָחוֹמֶר מִגֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the imagined picture from step 26 by showing how the עבד would be covered.
steps.raayaObject: That the imagined wording would leave nothing out
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the גר to the עבד

steps.title: The actual wording shows only the slave is unfit
steps.stepSummary: Since the Torah actually wrote ״אָבוֹת עַל בָּנִים״ without 'their', it teaches that someone with no family link to children cannot testify. That is the עבד, who has no link in either direction. A גר, who has a link downward, is fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the Torah wrote 'Fathers shall not be put to death for children', which means people are not killed through the testimony of fathers who have no family link to their children, we learn that the עבד, who has no family link upward or downward, is the one who is unfit. A גר has a family link downward, so he is fit to testify.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof. The real wording of the פסוק shows that the עבד is unfit and the גר is fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the פסוק, ״אָבוֹת עַל בָּנִים״, is read as 'fathers with no family link to children'. That points to someone with no downward link, which a גר has but an עבד lacks. If a גר were unfit, this lesson would be unnecessary, as steps 26 and 27 showed. So the line is drawn at the עבד.
steps.whatToRemember: A גר is a valid witness because he is related to his children. An עבד is not, because he has no recognized family link upward or downward.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical הלכה that a גר may testify while an עבד may not, and it shows how one missing word, 'their', carries the lesson.

phrases.english: Rather, since the Merciful One wrote:
"Fathers shall not be put to death for children"

phrases.aramaic: דְּמַשְׁמַע: לֹא יוּמְתוּ עַל פִּי אָבוֹת
phrases.english: which means: people are not put to death through the testimony of fathers
who have no family link to children,

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ, עֶבֶד, שֶׁאֵין לוֹ חַיִיס
phrases.english: learn from this: a slave, who has no family link
neither upward nor downward,
he is the one who is unfit to testify;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל גֵּר, כֵּיוָן דְּיֵשׁ לוֹ חַיִיס לְמַטָּה –
phrases.english: but a convert, since he has a family link downward,
is fit to testify.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts the imagined wording from steps 26 and 27 with the actual wording and draws the conclusion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: An עבד, with no family link in either direction, is unfit to testify; a גר, linked to his children, is fit.

steps.title: Why does the second half also leave out 'their'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the Torah could have written ״עַל אֲבוֹתֵיהֶם״ in the second half. Why write ״עַל אָבוֹת״, which suggests children with no family link to fathers, meaning converts, are unfit?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: let the Torah write 'Nor shall children be put to death for their fathers'. Why did the Torah write 'for fathers', which suggests people are not killed through the testimony of children who have no family link to fathers?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem with the conclusion. The second half of the פסוק also leaves out 'their', and by the same reading it would seem to make a גר unfit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 28 learned a lot from the missing 'their' in the first half. The same word is missing in the second half, and reading it the same way points to a גר, which goes against the conclusion that a גר is fit. So why didn't the Torah write ״אֲבוֹתֵיהֶם״?

phrases.english: And if you will say: let the Merciful One write:
"Nor shall children be put to death for their fathers";
why do I need what the Merciful One wrote:
"Nor shall children be put to death for fathers"

phrases.aramaic: דְּמַשְׁמַע: לֹא יוּמְתוּ עַל פִּי בָּנִים
phrases.english: which means: people are not put to death through the testimony of children
who have no family link to fathers?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 28 by pointing to the same missing word in the second half of the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording ״עַל אָבוֹת״ in the second half of the פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a missing 'their' teaches a lesson in the first half, it should teach one in the second half too. That lesson would make a גר unfit, which contradicts step 28.

steps.title: The second half simply matches the first
steps.stepSummary: Because the first half was written ״אָבוֹת עַל בָּנִים״ without 'their', the Torah wrote the second half the same way, ״עַל אָבוֹת״, to match. No separate lesson comes from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the Torah wrote 'Fathers shall not be put to death for children', it also wrote 'Nor shall children be put to death for fathers'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the second half's wording just follows the style of the first half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lesson comes only from the first half. The second half was written to match it, so no extra teaching about a גר is drawn from it. That keeps the conclusion that a גר is fit.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, because of, meaning one wording follows from the other

steps.whatToRemember: Only the first half of the פסוק teaches the rule about the עבד. The second half's wording simply matches the first, so a גר stays fit to testify.

phrases.english: Since it wrote:
"Fathers shall not be put to death for children,"
it also wrote:
"Nor shall children be put to death for fathers."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Matching wording: the second phrase follows the style of the first, so no separate lesson is drawn from it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The missing 'their' in the second half teaches that a גר is unfit
steps.terutzMaskana: The second half's wording only matches the first half, so a גר remains fit to testify

steps.title: Back to the משנה: dealing with a deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, or a minor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line of the משנה saying that a run-in with a חרש, שוטה or קטן is bad for the other person.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: a deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person and a minor are bad to run into.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new section by quoting the next line of the משנה. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, 'bad to run into' means that if you hurt one of them you must pay, but if one of them hurts you, they are פטור. The גמרא quotes the line here only to tie the coming story to it.

keyTerms.meaning: A deaf-mute. In הלכה he is treated as lacking full legal responsibility.
A person who is mentally incompetent.
A minor, a child below the age of מצוות.
Literally, 'meeting them is bad': you pay if you hurt them, but they do not pay if they hurt you.

steps.confusionAlert: 'Bad to run into' does not mean these people are bad. It only means a legal run-in with them is a losing deal for the other person.

phrases.english: A deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, and a minor:
an encounter with them is bad.
phrases.notes: As the משנה explains, you pay if you injure them, but they're exempt if they injure you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the topic of a גר's testimony and goes back to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever injures a חרש, שוטה or קטן must pay, but if they injure others they are פטור.

steps.title: A mother signs her property over to her son
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a story. The mother of רב שמואל בר אבא, married to רבי אבא, wrote her property over to her son, and then she died.
steps.simpleTranslation: The mother of רב שמואל בר אבא from הגרוניא was married to רבי אבא. She wrote her property over to her son, רב שמואל בר אבא. After she died...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the facts of a story about a married woman who gave her property to her son. The story continues in the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two people are involved here: her husband, רבי אבא, and her son, רב שמואל בר אבא. She signed her property over to the son while she was married, and the words 'after she died' prepare us for what happened to that property next.

keyTerms.meaning: She wrote them over, meaning she signed them over in writing.

phrases.aramaic: אִימֵּיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אַבָּא מֵהַגְרוֹנְיָא
phrases.english: The mother of רב שמואל בר אבא from הגרוניא
was married to רבי אבא.
She wrote over her property
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording, 'her property.'

phrases.english: to רב שמואל בר אבא, her son.
After she died,

steps.triggerLanguage: אִימֵּיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אַבָּא מֵהַגְרוֹנְיָא הֲוָת נְסִיבָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After quoting the משנה, the גמרא opens a story that it will connect to this topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Facts of the case: a married woman signed her property over to her son, and then she died.
